diagnostic_reports.conclusion: CRITICAL FINDINGS: Severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction at 22% (prior baseline 35%). Global hypokinesia. Moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation. Dilated left ventricle. Right ventricular function mildly impaired. Small pericardial effusion. Findings consistent with acute-on-chronic decompensated systolic heart failure. Urgent cardiology input required. Cardiac ICU transfer recommended.

CRITICAL FINDINGS: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with hospital-acquired pneumonia. Bilateral pleural effusions — moderate right, small left. No pulmonary embolism identified. Cardiomegaly with pulmonary venous congestion. Air bronchograms within the consolidation. Clinical picture supports concurrent pneumonia and cardiogenic pulmonary oedema — dual pathology requiring concurrent aggressive management.

CRITICAL ANOMALIES DOCUMENTED: (1) Troponin I 4820 ng/L — NSTEMI cannot be excluded; cardiology team to perform urgent catheterisation risk-benefit assessment. (2) Haemoglobin 6.1 g/dL — active packed red cell transfusion underway; bone marrow cause vs chronic disease vs haemolysis under investigation. (3) Vasopressor dependency (norepinephrine 0.1 mcg/kg/min) — haemodynamically unstable. (4) INR 2.8 — bleeding risk limits invasive procedures. Patient requires multi-disciplinary ICU management.
